findings.text: follow-on: the absence scan widened from the raw tier to every tier now lexes a minute or hour file that carries no parseable row on every ingest pass until it settles. _holds_a_record_line stops at the first line that parses, so a settled tier costs one line and the cost is bounded by the file, which is at most the size of the tier the ingest already reads; it is recorded, not raised, because a pathologically large all-unparseable minute or hour file would pay a full read per pass where the previous raw-only predicate returned immediately.

follow_ons.text: The parse-based absence scan, widened from the raw tier to every tier, runs per discovered tier file per ingest pass; a minute or hour file whose every line fails to parse is lexed until it settles. Bounded by the file and unchanged for the common settled case (the scan stops at the first parsing line), so recorded rather than raised.
